tdd_audit: All 7 steps are tdd:true with tdd_evidence present and a test_cmd; no tdd:false scaffolding step carries business logic. No escape-hatch findings.

issues.summary: post_pull attaches the FULL weeks_verified_empty list to every chunk payload while weeks_complete is only that chunk's weeks. validateIngest_ (Code.gs:238-247) rejects any payload whose weeks_verified_empty entry is absent from that request's weeks_complete, so as soon as a pull needs more than one data chunk AND any spanned week returned zero rows, the first chunk is rejected with 'weeks_verified_empty entry not in weeks_complete' and the whole pull aborts with IngestFailed (no data, no pull marker). Reproduced: 450 rows over 3 weeks + verified-empty 2026-W31 -> chunks 1 and 2 declare weeks_complete=['2026-W28']/['2026-W29'] but still carry weeks_verified_empty=['2026-W31']. step2.md explicitly warns 'each request is validated alone'. Fix: emit weeks_verified_empty only on the chunk whose chunk_weeks contains it.
issues.test_gap: test_ingest.py:452 covers the single-chunk case only; no test combines a verified-empty week with a multi-chunk span.

issues.summary: Silent row loss regression: when weeks_complete is non-empty, packing iterates only over weeks_complete, so any dated_row whose week_label is not in weeks_complete is never posted to any request and no warning is printed. Before this phase every mapped row was posted unconditionally. Reproduced: rows for 2026-W99 + 2026-W28 with weeks_complete=['2026-W28'] -> only the W28 row reaches _send, the other is dropped with no stderr output and no non-zero exit. Contrast the split-week path, which at least warns. Fix: post leftover out-of-declaration weeks in undeclared chunks (same shape as the split_weeks loop), or fail loud.

iso_week_span always rolls over at week 53, so a span crossing into a 52-week ISO year emits a nonexistent label — iso_week_span('2025-W51','2026-W02') returns ['2025-W51','2025-W52','2025-W53','2026-W01','2026-W02']. The phantom week is declared complete and (having no rows) verified-empty. Harmless downstream today (GAS finds no rows for it, so no candidates), but it inflates weeks_verified_empty and therefore the blast radius of the multi-chunk bug above. Use datetime.date.fromisocalendar / isocalendar() to determine the real last week of each year.

self._redact(detail) assumes detail is a str. The API's `detail` field is untrusted JSON; if it arrives as a dict or list the redaction call raises AttributeError ('dict' object has no attribute 'replace') from inside the fatal-error path, replacing the clean ShopSpendError with an opaque crash. No token is leaked by the AttributeError, so this is robustness, not disclosure. Coerce with str(detail) before redacting.

Three of the six completeness-gate branches return ([], []) with no operator-visible message: len(rows) < paging.matched, diag.totalOrdersScanned == 0, and diag.emptyRangeWithInvalidLabels. The paging-None and matched==0 branches both warn, and truncated is warned at line 217, so the omission is inconsistent rather than deliberate. Tombstoning is silently disabled for that pull; it is only recoverable by reading diagnostics_json.harness in the Sheet. Add a stderr WARNING to each, matching the existing two.

Diagnostics honesty gap that step 3 ('pull-diagnostics-honest-values') did not close: `returned` is written as paging.returned, which is the FIRST page's count only, while `matched` is the total and response.rows holds every page. Any paginated pull therefore records returned < matched in ShopSpendPulls and reads as truncated when it was complete. No code consumes column 5 today (shopSpendReportBlock_ reads 0, 8, 9, 12, 13, 15, 16), so this is a reporting lie, not a logic bug. Write len(response.rows).

Docs overstate what weeks_verified_empty asserts: 'the caller asserting it positively confirmed the week is empty upstream, not merely I saw fewer rows than before'. compute_weeks_complete derives it purely as span_weeks - returned_weeks — absence of rows behind a passing global gate, not a per-week positive confirmation. The behaviour is a deliberate, documented design choice (step1.md:110, :220), but a reader of docs/api.md will over-trust the exemption. Reword to describe the gate that actually backs it.

A 914-line pytest/node run log was committed to the repository root. .gitignore covers logs/ but not a root-level *.log, so this build artifact is now tracked history. Delete it and extend .gitignore, or move it under phases/shopspend-hardening/ with the other step logs.
